p: Dundee has a proper science and invention streak, and you can follow it well beyond Greenmarket. Up on Balgay Hill, the Mills Observatory was the UK's first purpose-built public observatory, and on winter evenings it has a long tradition of letting visitors peer through its telescope when the sky is clear. It's a lovely follow-up for kids who enjoyed the space side of things.

The city also has a big claim in the video games world. Lemmings and the original Grand Theft Auto were both developed here, and Dundee is still home to a busy games industry. Gamers in the family will enjoy knowing that, and the V&A Dundee has featured design work from the sector in the past.

Industrial history fans should head for Verdant Works, a former jute mill turned museum that tells the story of the textile trade that made the city. The McManus, a grand Victorian gallery and museum in the centre, covers Dundee's history and art and is free to wander.

Keep your eyes peeled in the city centre too. Dundee is the home of comic publisher DC Thomson, and you'll find bronze statues of Desperate Dan and Minnie the Minx from The Dandy and The Beano, perfect for a cheeky family photo.

For fresh air, Broughty Ferry is a short hop east, with a sandy beach, a castle by the water and plenty of spots for chips or an ice cream. Or climb the Law, the old volcanic hill in the middle of the city, for views over the Tay and its famous bridges. On a dreich day, though, the science centre and a museum or two will happily fill your time indoors.
